text:
Alex Ovechkin walks into Ottawa tonight with a protest waiting outside. Ukrainian Canadians plan to demonstrate at the arena over his ties to Vladimir Putin, The Globe and Mail reported. That's the story of this game. On the ice, he arrives in the deepest dry spell of his season: no goals in ten games on 3.6 expected goals (the quality of his chances), and no points in seven straight. The looks are there. Our numbers give him a 23% chance to score.

The rest of Washington's week has been loud too. Tom Wilson avoided a suspension for the boarding hit that injured Florida's Sandis Vilmanis and got him ejected Saturday (DAZN, RMNB). Alex Tuch, whose exit from Buffalo has turned into a public back-and-forth with the Sabres' GM (Yahoo Sports), is the most likely scorer on either side at 39%, on the Tuch-Strome-Kyrou line, the only one Tom Gulitti of NHL.com reported intact after last week's shuffle. Ryan Leonard plays his 100th NHL game. Logan Thompson (projected) is at +1.9 goals saved above expected after a +28.2 season.

Ottawa gets a body back: Ridly Greig says he'll return tonight (Sportsnet). The Senators need him. William Eklund is on injured reserve with an ankle injury (ESPN estimates early January), and Andre Burakovsky and Warren Foegele are out three to four weeks. Since Eklund went down, Tim Stützle has slid beside Dylan Cozens and Fabian Zetterlund, and Ottawa has won the chance battle in four of its last five. Samuel Ersson (projected) was 17.8 goals below expected last season but has saved 3.9 above it over his last five starts. With Linus Ullmark back at practice, this feels like an audition Ersson can't afford to lose.

Our numbers can barely split them: 3.22 expected goals for Ottawa, 3.18 for Washington, and 54% against 52% of the five-on-five chances. Watch the penalty box. The Senators draw 5.2 penalties a game and take 4.7, the Capitals take 4.4, and Ottawa's power play (0.76 expected goals a game) meets a Washington kill that allows 0.87.
headline: Ovechkin, a protest and a coin flip in Ottawa

hunch.text: Our hunch: Ovechkin ends the drought tonight. Ten games of good chances without a goal is a streak, not a decline, and a loud night in a rival building feels like the kind he answers.
